thread:
Alex K: Heads-up — after the 2.3.0 kernel bump we saw ~6% drop in prompt-cache hit rate for /chat and /complete. Starting a quick triage, posting profiler snapshots.
Maria P: oof, across all models or just the larger ones?
Alex K: Mostly the medium Llama family in us-west. Noticed higher eviction churn in kv-cache slab metrics. Perf bot linked below.
perf-bot: [profile] https://perf.internal/runs/2026-03-17/173823 - edge: saw increased KV eviction during batching window (p95 batch_size 4 -> 6)
Chen L: Could kernel change have altered how we compute prefix fingerprints? We recently switched to xxhash64 + salt for streaming stability.
Ravi S: I compared keys: the salted-hash -> different values for identical prompt pairs when system prompt had trailing newline. Small normalization diff.
Kaitlyn T: Wait, did we change prompt sanitizer behavior in 2.3.0? I remember a microfix that trimmed consecutive spaces differently.
Alex K: Yup — sanitizer now collapses repeated spaces but preserves trailing newline. Prior runtime trimmed trailing newline. That plus salt explains mismatches.
Maria P: So same user text but two canonicalizations -> cache miss. Can we patch sanitizer or make hash ignore trailing newlines? Which is safer for semantics?
Chen L: For most models trailing newline is semantically neutral, but there are edgecases with system prompts that rely on a newline to separate instructions. We shouldn't silently drop it.
Ravi S: Option A: normalize newline only for user messages, keep system prompt verbatim. Option B: include sanitizer version in cache key so keys aren't magically incompatible.
Kaitlyn T: Also flagging tokenizer pinning: some callers started sending tokenizer_version: "v2.2" vs "v2.1" after SDK bump. Keys include tokenizer_version right now.
Alex K: That's critical — SDK change will fragment cache. We have thousands of keys split by minor tokenizer metadata.
Maria P: Proposal: key components = [model, canonicalized_user_prompt, canonicalized_system_prompt OR hashed-system-version, tokenizer_pin, tool-call-map]. But we should make tokenizer_pin optional fallback.
Chen L: I'd rather we canonicalize tool calls deterministically (sort keys, stable JSON) and then canonicalize. Right now tool args order is preserved which causes misses when frontends reorder args.
Ravi S: Agreed. Example we saw: {"tool":"lookup","args":{"q":"x","lang":"en"}} vs {"args":{"lang":"en","q":"x"}} -> different key
Kaitlyn T: Quick mitigation: add compatibility layer for keys produced in last 30 days and backfill hot prefixes into new keyspace for top-1000 keys.
Alex K: Backfill sounds heavy but doable for hot prefixes. For immediate fix — roll a tiny patch: revert sanitizer trailing newline change for user messages and deploy canary to 10% traffic.
perf-bot: Canary deploy started: 1738240000 -> traffic 10% to sanitizer-v2. Realtime metrics will appear in 10m.
Maria P: Also open a short-term change: stop including tokenizer_version in cache key if caller didn't explicitly pin it (i.e., null/absent)
Chen L: We should log when tokenizer not pinned and issue a warning to SDK callers. Long-term: add a key-version field to allow rolling changes without accidental invalidation.
Ravi S: On batching heuristics — profiler shows increased mean batch size due to kernel's adjusted queue timeout. Larger batches increased contention for KV slab leading to eviction spikes.
Alex K: Lowering batch wait to previous value reduced p95 latency slightly but brought batch efficiency down. We need a smarter policy: prefer lower-latency routing for cache-warm prefixes.
Kaitlyn T: Idea: label requests with "hot-prefix" when prior LRU counter indicates frequent hits. Hot-prefix requests route to steady nodes with larger reserved kv egress.
Maria P: That needs simulation. Can we run replay on yesterdays traffic and mark top 5% prefixes as hot and simulate routing? I can spin that in replay infra.
Alex K: Please do. Action items: (1) Revert trailing-newline sanitizer for user messages (canary 10%) — Alex. (2) Deprecate tokenizer_version in key when absent + warn SDK — Maria. (3) Stable canonicalization for tool args (sort keys) — Chen. (4) Backfill hot prefixes for top-1000 keys — Ravi/Kaitlyn. (5) Run replay for hot-prefix routing simulation — Maria.
Kaitlyn T: I'll start backfill plan doc and estimate storage cost.
Ravi S: I'll prepare extraction of current hot keys and a small operator job to copy them to new keys.
Alex K: Thanks team. Let's plan to reconvene in 2 hours with first canary metrics. :thumbsup:
